name: Dextrin
description: Dextrin (CAS 9004-53-9 ), also known commercially as E1400 , is a starch-derived carbohydrate produced through partial hydrolysis or thermal treatment of starch. It functions as a binder, adhesive, thickener, and carrier across food, industrial, and pharmaceutical manufacturing. In food production, E1400 acts as a bulking agent and encapsulation carrier for flavors, oils, and spray-dried ingredients. This improves the shelf stability and flowability of finished powders in various commercial applications. Corrugated board, paper bag, and envelope manufacturing rely on dextrin-based adhesives for their fast-tack, water-based bonding performance. These industrial solutions provide reliable adhesion for high-speed production lines. Textile and printing operations use it as a thickener in screen printing pastes and a sizing agent to improve fabric stiffness. This process enhances yarn processability and ensures consistent quality in textile finishing. In pharmaceutical tablet and capsule manufacturing, it functions as a binder and diluent, supporting granulation and controlled disintegration. It is a critical component for ensuring the structural integrity of medicinal dosages. Dextrin is supplied as a white to off-white powder, with granulated forms available for specific industrial applications. Established grades include food-grade ( FCC compliant), pharmaceutical-grade ( USP / BP ), and technical-grade. Conversion degree and solubility profiles vary by grade, so buyers typically specify dextrin type based on application requirements.
